codeReview.summary: Fix review of fnd-fix-domain-contract-compliance (abcd2071, parent 452bb463; the tree at HEAD d835bc9e is byte-identical for packages/reservations). Verified against the prior review (fnd-zoned-time-and-reservations-domain) and the current tree. Adjudication of the 8 prior blocking findings: (1) RESOLVED - 'hard-lock arrived ... in isBookingHardLocked'; HARD_LOCKED_STATUSES at engine/day-state.ts:143-149 now covers partially_arrived/arrived/partially_seated/seated/finished and isBookingHardLocked (day-state.ts:157-172) is the single hard-lock source: occupancy entries carry it (engine/assign.ts:370-388), 1-step/2-step repair refuses hardLocked owners (assign.ts:680,688,756,765,791,800), reflowDay splits hard/soft with the same predicate (assign.ts:960-973); regression test assign.test.ts:321-368 covers arrived + partially_arrived for both planBooking and reflow. (2) PARTIAL - 'must be search 200 per slot, book 2,000, reflow 5,000, with no fit/budgetExhausted rather than partial plans'. The three constants are now correct (assign.ts:23-27: MAX_SEARCH_SLOT_EXPANSIONS=200, MAX_BOOK_EXPANSIONS=2,000, MAX_REFLOW_EXPANSIONS=5,000), assignTables caps at 2,000 (assign.ts:467-470) and reflowDay at 5,000 (assign.ts:942-945), search caps each slot at 200 (engine/availability.ts:539-544), and the day-level reflow exhaustion path now returns a full reset (status 'no_fit', budgetExhausted: true, original assignments, moves []) (assign.ts:998-1003, 1151-1184), proven by scale.test.ts:118-159. However reflowDay still gives each nested placement only MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS=200 (assign.ts:1079, Math.min(MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS, remainingBudget)); when that sub-budget is hit while the 5,000 day budget is not, the booking is pushed to unresolvable and the loop continues (assign.ts:1137-1148), so a reflow call returns a partially applied plan (some bookings moved in `moves`, the rest resolved, status 'no_fit', budgetExhausted: false) - the architecture forbids this: 'Exhausting a budget returns "no fit" (never a partial plan)' (architecture.md:1196-1197) and the normative research puts a booking-placement search on the book budget (research/reservation-engineering.md:204-206, 274-276), bounded by the caller's 5,000. This is reachable in the contract's own 120-table/80-combination fixture: a single repair attempt iterates roughly 150 occupied candidates (72 tables fitting party 4 + 80 combinations) in the 1-step loop alone, so >200-expansion attempts occur and scale.test.ts:86-100 does not assert `unresolvable.length === 0`. (3) RESOLVED - validateConfig returns ConfigIssue[] (config/validate.ts:175-190, 696-716, array with non-enumerable .valid/.issues/.errors/.warnings so old report reads still work), strict blocks schema (config/index.ts:538-590 blockSchema/tableBlockSchema, 592-604 locationConfigSchema includes blocks/policies) and policyRuleSchema superRefines (480-536), contiguous 1..party_max bucket coverage incl. leading/middle/trailing gaps (validate.ts:524-587), end_min - first_seating_min <= 1440 and last_seating bounds (validate.ts:434-476; also config/index.ts serviceSchema/customServiceEntrySchema superRefines), invalid policy references (validate.ts:621-668), block window/table checks (670-698); new tests config.test.ts:499-591 assert Array.isArray and each code. (4) RESOLVED - localToInstant(date, localMin, tz, opts) with gap 'skip'|'after' and overlap 'earlier'|'later' (time.ts:48-61, 93-167; null only for gap 'skip', time.ts:156-158), resolveServiceWindow uses gap 'after'/overlap 'earlier' for the start and overlap 'later' for the end (time.ts:227-253), search slots call gap 'skip' and skip null (availability.ts:501-510); time.test.ts:12-174 pins the contract dates 2027-03-14 NY/LA, 2027-03-28 London, 2026-11-01 NY/LA, 2026-10-25 London, the 90-minute fold 01:15 -> second 01:45, day_start_min 240 +/- 1 and Asia/Riyadh midnight crossing. (5) RESOLVED - BOOKING_CHANNELS/isGuestChannel (day-state.ts:5-31) covers online/native/voice_agent/phone/host/walk_in/waitlist (+legacy operator/voice), walk_in_only allowed only for walk_in/waitlist (day-state.ts:128-141, buildCandidates walkInOnly default mode), and staff channels keep pacing-breached slots with per-slot warnings plus a day-level warnings list instead of dropping them (availability.ts:530-537, 594-604, 618, 638); tests availability.test.ts:344-445. (6) RESOLVED - strict deadline response schemas with ISO expiresAt + server now: createHoldResponseSchema/largePartyRequestResponseSchema/notifyMeOfferResponseSchema (schemas/public.ts:107-141), waitlistOfferResponseSchema (schemas/waitlist.ts:51-60), paymentSessionResponseSchema (schemas/payments.ts:53-66), common isoTimestampSchema/deadlineResponseFields (schemas/common.ts:11-22), all re-exported via schemas/index.ts and package root; tests schemas.test.ts:191-270. (7) PARTIAL - 'extend verifyDayInvariants ... to check all invariants I1 through I8 and update engine.property.test.ts to run random operation sequences ... verifying I1-I8 after every step'. The harness part is implemented (arbitraryOperationSequence arbitraries.ts:520-554 all 11 named ops, executeOperationSequence :556-954, verifyDayInvariants called after every step :935-947; engine.property.test.ts:128-147) and I5 is now genuinely verified (oracle.ts:202-227). But the invariant set that must be checked is incomplete: no check that a searched slot can be held (I7 in architecture.md:236-237; skill SKILL.md step 3 calls it I6), no monotonic-release check (I8 architecture.md:238-239; skill I7), no atomic-modify check (I6 architecture.md:234-235; skill I8) - the modify op only applies engine results when they succeed (arbitraries.ts:722-766), so a partial mutation cannot surface, and engine.property.test.ts:115-117 only asserts slot.tableIds.length > 0; staff-overbook isolation (I3) is also not exercised. The oracle instead attaches I6/I7/I8 labels to pacing caps (oracle.ts:229-261), channel/mode eligibility (oracle.ts:76-177) and interval/service-window checks (oracle.ts:78-81, 179-199), i.e. a fourth numbering that matches neither architecture.md 6.6 (I6 atomic modify, I7 search/book agreement, I8 monotonic release) nor library/engine-notes.md:210 nor skills/domain-worker/SKILL.md step 3 (I6 any searched slot can be held, I7 cancel/finish/release never decreases availability, I8 failed modification changes nothing). The handoff claims 'check all invariants I1 through I8' and skillFeedback.followedProcedure=true with no deviations, which overstates the delivery. (8) RESOLVED - weekly service templates now carry priority and sort by latest effectiveFrom descending then priority descending (rules/resolve-services.ts:96-97, 165-197, 252-261), tested in resolve-services.test.ts:240-281. Downstream alignment items also verified: quiet hours default 21:00-08:00 with move-earlier/skip for pre-arrival reminders (messages.ts:111, 187-228; messages.test.ts), MESSAGE_KINDS matches architecture.md 9.3 exactly (18 kinds), state-machine RESERVATION_STATUSES matches 6.4 with pending_payment capacity until payment_expires_at and requested only when request_holds_capacity (state-machine.ts:6-77). Regression checks: no repository consumer outside packages/reservations imports validateConfig, BookingChannel, resolveServices/ResolvedService, assignTables/reflow results or localToInstant (rg over apps/ and packages/ found only permissions/flags/token/phone/context schema imports), so the changed return type, widened channel union and new sort/time behavior break no call sites; time.ts callers inside the package either handle null (availability.ts:507-510) or pass no opts (messages.ts, experiences.ts, arbitraries.ts); tenant-db/tenant-api status vocabulary lags the new canonical statuses but there is no DB CHECK constraint and typecheck passes (recorded as a shared-state observation). Two of eight prior blocking findings are only partially satisfied, so this fix still fails.

issues.description: Finding 2 residual: reflowDay still caps each nested placement at MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS = 200 (`maxExpansions: Math.min(MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS, remainingBudget)`, assign.ts:1079) even though the reflow call now has a 5,000-expansion budget (assign.ts:942-945). When that 200 sub-budget is exhausted while totalExpansions < maxExpansions, the code marks the booking unresolvable and continues (assign.ts:1137-1148) instead of returning the day-budget no-fit reset (assign.ts:1151-1184), so reflow can return a partially applied plan (successful `moves` for other bookings, `unresolvable` for the failed one, `status: 'no_fit'`, `budgetExhausted: false`). Architecture.md:1196-1197 requires 'Exhausting a budget returns "no fit" (never a partial plan)', and the normative research gives a booking placement the book budget (research/reservation-engineering.md:204-206, 274-276) bounded by the caller's reflow budget. Reachable in the contract's own 120-table/80-combination fixture (one repair attempt iterates ~150 occupied candidates in its 1-step loop), and scale.test.ts:86-100 asserts only `expansions <= 5,000` / `budgetExhausted === false`, never `unresolvable.length === 0`, so the partial path has no regression coverage. Suggested fix: pass min(MAX_BOOK_EXPANSIONS, remainingBudget) into the nested assignTables call (or treat any nested budget exhaustion as the reflow-level no-fit reset), and assert a successful reflow has an empty `unresolvable` in the scale test.

Finding 7 residual: the property suite verifies a set of invariants after every step (arbitraries.ts:520-954, engine.property.test.ts:128-147) but not the required I1-I8 semantics. There is no search-then-hold check (engine.property.test.ts:115-117 only asserts returned slots have tableIds), no monotonic-release check (nothing compares availability before/after cancel/seat/finish), and no atomic-modify check (the modify operation applies results only when assignTables succeeds, arbitraries.ts:722-766, so a partial mutation is invisible); overbook isolation is likewise unexercised. The oracle's labels are attached to unrelated properties: oracle.ts:229-261 labels pacing caps as I6, oracle.ts:76-177 labels channel/mode eligibility as I7, and oracle.ts:78-81/179-199 labels interval/service-window checks as I8, whereas architecture.md:234-239 defines I6 atomic modify, I7 search/book agreement ('any slot returned by a search can be held immediately'), I8 monotonic release, and skills/domain-worker/SKILL.md step 3 requires the same three semantics (numbered I6/I7/I8 differently). VAL-FND-009 requires 'invariants I1 through I8 after every step', so the clause is only partially met and the handoff's 'check all invariants I1 through I8' claim is not accurate. Suggested fix: add per-step checks (hold a searched slot against identical state/clock; compare availability before/after cancel/finish/shrink; assert failed modify leaves the reservation untouched) and relabel the oracle to the mission's canonical invariant list.

Overload soundness hole: `localToInstant(date, min, tz, opts?: LocalToInstantOptions): LocalInstantResolution` (time.ts:99-104) claims a non-null result for a widened options variable, but the implementation can return null when opts.gap === 'skip' (time.ts:156-158). Only the literal-options overload (time.ts:93-98) is nullable. No current call site passes a widened variable (availability.ts:501-505 passes a literal, handled correctly), so this is latent; a caller forwarding `opts` through a variable would get a compile-time non-null type and a runtime TypeError on `.instantMs`.

Legacy constants keep a competing budget vocabulary: MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS (200) and MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS (2,000) are still exported (assign.ts:24,26); MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS is now unused in src (only asserted in assign.test.ts:14,402,481) and MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS survives only as the reflow sub-budget (assign.ts:1079). Two names for the same numbers is what caused the original mis-mapping; consider deleting MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS and renaming/removing MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS once the reflow budget issue above is resolved.

Leading and trailing 1..party_max bucket coverage gaps are reported with severity 'warning' (validate.ts:526-537, 574-586), consistent with the pre-existing middle-gap severity (validate.ts:556-568), so `valid` remains true for an incomplete bucket table. VAL-FND-004 only requires validateConfig to detect and report the issue, so this is noted for the validator's judgement, not as a defect; a stricter reading of 'fail to cover 1..party_max' might prefer 'error'.

On the day-budget reset path, `unresolvable` and `unassignedIds` are set to every soft booking id (assign.ts:1171-1179) even though those bookings still hold their original tables (assignments returns the unchanged originals). Callers must not read `unassignedIds` as 'occupancy released'; a distinct field or an empty list with a 'day unchanged' status would be less ambiguous for the host-stand milestone.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The mission carries at least three different I1-I8 definitions, which is why the fix's oracle invented a fourth mapping: architecture.md 6.6 (I6 atomic modify, I7 search/book agreement, I8 monotonic release), library/engine-notes.md:210 (same as architecture), and skills/domain-worker/SKILL.md step 3 (I6 any searched slot can be held, I7 cancel/finish/release never decreases availability, I8 a failed modification changes nothing). The delivered oracle labels I6 = pacing caps, I7 = channel/mode eligibility, I8 = interval/service window. Pick one canonical list and make architecture, library, skill and tests agree; otherwise every future property-test review re-litigates the numbering.

skills/domain-worker/SKILL.md step 3 already spells out the required random operation sequence and invariant list, but the worker shipped an oracle that verifies different semantics and reported skillFeedback.followedProcedure=true with an empty deviations list (handoff 2026-10-16T04-13-40). The skill itself is adequate; what is missing is a verification obligation - e.g. require the handoff to map each named invariant to the oracle line/test that asserts it - so 'followedProcedure: true' cannot paper over a partial invariant set.

The tenant DB status vocabulary is now out of step with the canonical state machine after this fix. packages/tenant-db/src/schema.ts:2954-2968 still defines RSV_RESERVATION_STATUS_VALUES with pending_approval/disputed and without requested/partially_arrived (used as the Drizzle enum for rsv_reservations.status at :3984 and rsv_reservation_events.from_status/to_status at :4212-4213), and apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-write.ts:274-279,318 still expires on 'pending_approval'. There is no DB CHECK constraint, so nothing fails today, but any typed write of 'requested'/'partially_arrived' through @repo/tenant-db will not compile until it is reconciled. Record the canonical 13 statuses in library/ (or staffing-patterns.md) so the DB/backend features pick them up.

No services gap: the fix worker only used commands that already exist in services.yaml (test_workspace for @repo/reservations and @repo/zoned-time, seeded FC_SEED vitest runs, typecheck_workspace for reservations/zoned-time/tenant-api plus the App typecheck, lint_oxc/oxlint and the Lingui check). No server, browser or port was started. The only notable extra is running the full App typecheck for a package-only commit, which is harmless over-verification.

summary: Fix abcd2071 (diff b10ef622..abcd2071 plus 452bb463 context; current tree for packages/reservations is unchanged by the later d835bc9e fix) resolves 6 of the 8 prior blocking findings outright (I5 hard-lock of arrived/partially_arrived and friends, validateConfig ConfigIssue[] with contiguous 1..party_max buckets / 1440-minute span / policy references / strict blocks schema, localToInstant gap 'skip'|'after' and overlap 'earlier'|'later' with all contract DST cases, full BookingChannel set with walk_in_only for walk_in+waitlist and staff pacing warnings, strict deadline response schemas with ISO expiresAt + server now, and weekly-template effectiveFrom/priority ordering) plus the quiet-hours/MESSAGE_KINDS/state-machine alignment, but two remain only partially satisfied, so the fix fails: (2) reflowDay's nested placement is still capped at 200 expansions (assign.ts:1079) and returns a partially applied plan with budgetExhausted=false when that sub-budget is exhausted (assign.ts:1137-1148), contrary to architecture.md:1196-1197 ('Exhausting a budget returns "no fit" (never a partial plan)') and the normative research's book-scale placement budget, with no regression test asserting an empty `unresolvable`; (7) the property suite now runs the required random operation sequences with per-step verification (and I5 is genuinely checked), but the required I1-I8 semantics are incomplete - no search-then-hold agreement (I7), no monotonic-release (I8) and no atomic-modify (I6) checks - while the oracle attaches those labels to pacing/channel/service-window checks and the handoff claims full I1-I8 coverage with followedProcedure=true and no deviations. No consumer regressions were found: no repository code outside packages/reservations imports the changed return types or unions, and the internal localToInstant callers all handle the new nullable overload correctly.
